title: Video-delivered group exercise for knee osteoarthritis in a rural physiotherapy service: a convergent mixed-methods evaluation
abstract: Objective: to describe outcomes and experiences of a six-week video group exercise programme for knee osteoarthritis in a rural service. Design: convergent mixed-methods evaluation. Quantitative strand: KOOS-12 change at three months for all starters and completion by subgroup. Qualitative strand: 16 to 20 interviews including non-completers. Results and conclusions will follow data collection.
introduction: Video-delivered exercise gives similar pain outcomes to in-person exercise in trials, but trial participants were younger and digitally connected. Rural services need to know whether their own participants benefit and who is left out.
methods: All starters from March 2026 to March 2027 contribute routine outcomes, with telephone follow-up of non-completers. Interviews are sampled for age, internet access, language and completion. Results are integrated in a joint display.
results: No data have been collected yet. The report will present KOOS-12 change, completion by subgroup, interview themes and the joint display.
discussion: The discussion will compare local outcomes with the trial evidence and set out which groups need an in-person or supported alternative.
limitations: Single group without comparison; missing outcomes for some non-completers; one service.
reportingChecklist: GRAMMS with COREQ for the interview strand
summary: Mixed-methods report structure with results left empty.
